events.title: Battle of Long Island
events.description: British forces under General William Howe defeated George Washington's Continental Army in present-day Brooklyn, New York. It was the largest battle of the American Revolutionary War. Members of the 1st Maryland Regiment repeatedly charged a much larger British force to cover the army's retreat.
events.significance: Washington's army escaped destruction and survived to keep fighting. The battle opened a campaign that cost the Americans New York City.

events.title: Edwin Drake Strikes Oil in Titusville
events.description: Edwin Drake successfully drilled for oil in Titusville, Pennsylvania. This was the first successful commercial oil well in the United States.
events.significance: The well set off the Pennsylvania oil rush and the first American oil boom. It helped launch the modern petroleum age.

events.title: Birth of Lyndon B. Johnson
events.description: Lyndon Baines Johnson was born on a farm in Gillespie County, Texas, near Johnson City. He later became the 36th President of the United States.
events.significance: As president from 1963 to 1969, Johnson signed major civil rights legislation and launched the Great Society programs.

events.title: Mariner 2 Launches to Venus
events.description: NASA launched the unmanned Mariner 2 spacecraft toward Venus.
events.significance: Mariner 2 became the first spacecraft to successfully fly past another planet. It showed that interplanetary exploration by robot probes was possible.

events.title: European Community Recognizes the Baltic States
events.description: The European Community recognized the independence of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. Moldova declared its independence from the Soviet Union on the same day.
events.significance: The recognition was a key moment in the collapse of the Soviet Union. It confirmed the return of the Baltic nations as sovereign states.
